title: Meromorphic module and the scalar map induced by a meromorphic section
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\mathcal M$ a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For an open $U$, let $\mathcal S(U)$ be the multiplicative subset of $\mathcal O_X(U)$ consisting of sections whose germ at each $x\in U$ is a non-zero-divisor in $\mathcal O_{X,x}$. Define $\mathcal K_X(\mathcal M)$ as the sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] of the presheaf $U\mapsto\mathcal S(U)^{-1}\mathcal M(U)$ with restriction $m/b\mapsto (m|_V)/(b|_V)$. Write $\mathcal K_X=\mathcal K_X(\mathcal O_X)$. The canonical map $\mathcal M\to\mathcal K_X(\mathcal M)$ sends $m$ to $m/1$, and the canonical local fraction maps send $m/b$ to its sheafification image. For an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module], this identifies $\mathcal K_X(\mathcal M)$ with $\mathcal K_X\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal M$. A global meromorphic section $s$ is equivalently an $\mathcal O_X$-linear morphism $\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal K_X(\mathcal M)$; it induces the unique $\mathcal O_X$-linear map $\mathcal K_X\to\mathcal K_X(\mathcal M)$ extending $s$, locally sending $a/b$ to $as/b$.

proof.text: Construct exists_meromorphicRestriction using LocalizedModule.liftOn. A witness a to equality of fractions restricts to restrictMeromorphicDenominator a; applying the semilinear restriction to the cross-multiplication equation proves well-definedness. Fraction induction and mk_add_mk and smul'_mk prove additivity and semilinearity.

The chosen restriction satisfies its fraction formula by choose_spec. Induction on fractions reduces meromorphicRestriction_id and meromorphicRestriction_comp to the ordinary module and ring presheaf laws. The fraction formula with denominator one proves meromorphicLocalization_natural.

Mathlib LocalizedModule.equivTensorProduct identifies the localization presheaf of M sectionwise with the tensor of the scalar localization presheaf and M. The inverse sends (a/b) tensor m to a times (m/b). Check naturality on such tensors using the proved fraction restriction equation. Sheafification is monoidal, and its counit at M is an isomorphism; applying its tensorator to this presheaf isomorphism proves meromorphicModule_tensor_iso. This argument in fact does not require invertibility, but preserves the existing signature.

For a denominator b on U, restrict to Over U. Its restrictions multiply localized sections invertibly, by IsLocalizedModule.map_units. The restricted sheafification unit is locally bijective. Its universal property transfers the inverse to the underlying presheaf of the associated sheaf: extend inv(a) followed by the unit, and verify both inverse equations by injectivity of precomposition with that unit. Evaluation at the identity of U proves b acts invertibly on sections of meromorphicModule M over U.

For s from the unit to meromorphicModule M, apply LocalizedModule.lift on every open using the preceding denominator invertibility. To check naturality on a/b, multiply both sides by the restricted b, use the localization cancellation formula, and apply naturality of s. The sheafification adjunction descends these compatible lifts to f. The lift formula at denominator one proves toMeromorphicModule followed by f is s. For any other extension, the adjunction and LocalizedModule.lift_unique identify its components with those lifts, proving unique existence.
